subject: Recap + MAP draft: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calls) - Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>, Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + MAP draft: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calls) - Acme

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: Integrate Redwood inference into Acme’s customer support flow for automated responses + tool calling to your order system.
- Key technical asks: SDK-based integration, low-latency streaming for chat, tool-calling to execute order lookups, and structured JSON outputs for downstream systems.
- Risks / dependencies: KMS access for keys, procurement timeline for dedicated capacity (if needed), and a sample of your structured output schema.

Attached is a first-pass MAP (ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.docx) and an Integration_Checklist.xlsx with proposed milestones. High-level proposed milestones:
  1) Sign MAP / Procurement kickoff (owner: Acme procurement) — target: 2026-02-05
  2) SDK integration PoC (owner: Redwood — Vivek) — target: 2026-02-19
  3) Streaming + tool-calling PoC (owner: Redwood — Dylan) — target: 2026-03-05
  4) Structured outputs validation (owner: Acme devs + Redwood — Neha) — target: 2026-03-12
  5) Final rollout / contract execution — target close: 2026-03-31

Please review the MAP draft and confirm: 1) owners above, 2) target close date, and 3) any additional dependencies we should add.

Next steps: If that looks good I’ll update the MAP with owners and send an updated mutual action plan with dates. Can you also share the JSON schema you’d like outputs to follow?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.docx (MAP draft), Integration_Checklist.xlsx (milestones)

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + MAP draft: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calls) - Acme

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick q's from our side: 

1) Streaming: We need sub-200ms token latency for interactive support — can Redwood guarantee that in a PoC on our infra or will we need Dedicated capacity?
2) Tool-calling: We’d like more detail on the security model for calling our order API (OAuth vs signed requests).
3) Procurement: Target close of 2026-03-31 works for our internal roadmap but I need to get procurement kickoff scheduled this week. I’ve looped in procurement@acme.com.

I’ve attached the procurement_form.pdf we usually use. Also looping in our engineering lead if they have follow-ups after you share the schema.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Product, Acme Corp
samir@acme.com

Attachments: procurement_form.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>, Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + MAP draft: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calls) - Acme

Thanks Samir — great questions. Quick answers and an updated owner assignment (I’ll push a revised MAP after we confirm schema):

- Streaming latency: For PoC we can run on Redwood hosted infra and achieve sub-200ms for typical short chats; if you want to run on your infra or guarantee under heavy load, Dedicated capacity is recommended. We’ll include a performance validation milestone in the MAP.
- Tool-calling security: We support OAuth and signed webhook requests; for sensitive actions we recommend OAuth + scoped service accounts and Redwood function-level scopes.

Owner assignments (proposed):
  - SDK integration PoC: Vivek Kulkarni (Redwood) — SDK, auth, sample app
  - Streaming & performance validation: Dylan Brooks (Redwood) — streaming config, latency testing, batching policy
  - Structured outputs / schema validation: Neha Kapoor (Redwood) + Acme eng lead (TBD)
  - Procurement & contract: Acme procurement (procurement@acme.com) + Marissa (commercial lead)

I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync next week for a short tech scoping call. Vivek / Dylan — can you review the checklist and give rough effort estimates? I put a HubSpot link to the record here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-42

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>, Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + MAP draft: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calls) - Acme

Looping in a quick technical readout based on the Integration_Checklist: 

- SDK integration (estimate): 2 engineer-weeks for PoC (sample app + auth + basic error handling). Key dependencies: API keys/KMS access, test account, and the sample JSON schema for outputs.
- Streaming: We’ll use Redwood Streaming SDK v2 (supports chunked output + reconnect). For sub-200ms median token latency in Hosted mode we should be fine for small-scale PoC; for production at scale plan on Dedicated capacity and the MAP will include a perf validation step.
- Tool-calling: Recommend using OAuth2 with short-lived tokens + Redwood function-level scopes. We’ll implement a sandbox function for PoC that hits a read-only order lookup endpoint.
- Structured outputs: We need a single canonical JSON schema (example keys: order_id, customer_id, action, confidence_score, metadata). Please share your concrete schema — that will reduce validation cycles.

Attachments: I added inline comments to Integration_Checklist.xlsx in the shared Drive (see link). I can take lead on SDK PoC workstream; Dylan — can you own streaming perf tests?

—Vivek
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>

Thanks team — attaching the sample schema we use for downstream systems: sample_schema.json.

We’re good with the proposed owners (Vivek/Dylan/Neha) and have kicked off procurement internally. I’ll confirm the Acme engineering lead (for schema validation) by EOD tomorrow. Please add a procurement milestone in the MAP and note any items you need from procurement (SOW, security questionnaire, billing contact).

—Samir

Attachments: sample_schema.json

Samir / team — thanks for the schema and confirmations. I’ve drafted a MAP timeline with milestones + owners below (I’ll push an updated ACME_MAP_Draft_v2.docx after we confirm procurement items):

- 2026-02-05: Procurement kickoff + SOW template sent (owner: Acme procurement, Marissa)
- 2026-02-19: SDK integration PoC complete (owner: Vivek)
- 2026-03-05: Streaming + tool-calling PoC complete (owner: Dylan)
- 2026-03-12: Structured outputs validation + test vectors (owner: Neha + Acme eng lead)
- 2026-03-18: Final validation + go/no-go review (owner: Marissa + Acme PM)
- 2026-03-31: Contract execution / target close (owner: Marissa + Acme procurement)

Dependencies: sample_schema.json (received), procurement form (received), dev test account & sandbox order API (Acme to provide).

Can everyone confirm the timeline and I’ll publish v2 of the MAP with milestone dates and owners. If Acme wants to accelerate any milestone, let us know and we’ll reprioritize resources.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
